clue.text: Writer considered time with murderer lacking credit

parts.note: to have felt something is to have considered or believed it

indicators.note: lacking says the following abbreviation is taken away from the killer's name

parts.note: Dr Crippen was a notorious Edwardian murderer hanged in 1910
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A writer weighs up an era spent with a killer who has no reputation left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' looks like an author but is a pen. Dr Crippen, the infamous wife-poisoner, loses CR to give IPPEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This marker with a fibre nib is an instrument for writing, so it is literally a writer.

clue.text: West Country town's former speaker

parts.note: ex- as a prefix means former, as in ex-wife
the mouth is the organ that does the speaking

explanation.surface: A town in the south-west of England once had a famous orator.
explanation.definitionFit: This seaside town lies at the mouth of the river Exe in Devon, in England's West Country.

clue.text: What some ancient citizens wore, so to speak?

definitions.meaning: Roman citizens wore loose woollen robes draped over the body
read as two words, '...', that is to chatter or talk at length

explanation.surface: A question about the clothing of classical Romans, with a wry aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' is a link: the second reading splits the answer into TO GAS, gas being slang for idle talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Romans of citizen rank wore these draped robes; split in two the word reads as an infinitive meaning to chatter.

clue.text: The Italian girl rings in a state

parts.note: il is the Italian word for the

indicators.note: rings means the girl's name encircles the next word

parts.note: Lois is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An Italian girl wearing rings is in a state of agitation.
explanation.definitionFit: This Midwestern territory, home to Chicago, is one of the fifty states of the USA.

clue.text: Play the clarinet badly (sic)

definitions.note: an aside written in brackets, as this Latin word is in the clue

indicators.note: badly signals that the first three words are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A stage direction telling a musician to perform poorly, with an editor's note.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the bracketed '(sic)': a word placed in parentheses in the clue itself is presented that way.
explanation.definitionFit: The bracketed word sic is set off within round brackets, which is the manner the adverb describes.

clue.text: Number one gets clear in case of necessity

indicators.note: in places the middle pieces inside the outer letters
the case of a word is its outside letters, its first and last

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to net is to clear as profit, net earnings being clear of costs

explanation.surface: Somebody first gets a clear way out when needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a cardinal number, nine tens.

clue.text: Impressionist scratching head, running back for plant

indicators.note: running back says the letters are read in reverse order
scratching the head strikes out the first letter

parts.note: Edgar Degas was a French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: A painter scratches his head and hurries back to the factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Sage is a herb, a grey-leaved aromatic plant used in cooking.

clue.text: Theologians terribly solemn about church organ at first

indicators.note: about means the anagram goes round the other pieces
terribly signals the next word's letters are scrambled
at first takes only the opening letter of organ

explanation.surface: Grave churchmen stand around a church organ, looking terribly serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval scholastic philosophers who taught divinity in the universities were known by this title.

clue.text: Sailors piercing screen for fish

indicators.note: piercing means one piece goes through the middle of the other

parts.note: a guard screens or shields something, as a fireguard does
RN, the Royal Navy, stands for sailors

explanation.surface: Seamen breaking through a barrier in search of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The gurnard is a bottom-dwelling sea fish with a large armoured head.

clue.text: Self-satisfied runner? Not half!

indicators.note: not half means only half of the word is kept, here the first four of eight letters

parts.note: a runner is one who smuggles goods, as in gunrunner or rum-runner

explanation.surface: Someone who thinks they're a fine athlete, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it means keep half of SMUGGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: Smug describes someone excessively pleased with themselves and complacent.

clue.text: Lyricist learning skill outside small country hotel

indicators.note: outside means the first two pieces are placed either side of the rest

parts.note: lore is traditional learning or knowledge
art is skill, as in the art of conversation
NZ is the abbreviation for New Zealand, a small country
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A songwriter studying craft outside a little hotel abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: He wrote the words for Richard Rodgers' songs, such as The Lady Is a Tramp.

clue.text: Dons backing down about leader of students?

indicators.note: backing means the whole construction is read in reverse
about means the phrase goes round the letter from students

parts.note: down is the opposite of up, so it is 'not up'

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: University teachers retreating in a mood over the head of the student body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dons' looks like Oxbridge tutors but is the verb, as in dons a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to put them on the body; the phrasal verb is the plain synonym.

clue.text: Reasonable notice required by US city in recession

indicators.note: in recession means going backwards, so the city name is reversed

parts.note: Boston is a city in Massachusetts
an ad is a notice in a newspaper

explanation.surface: An American city in economic downturn needs to post a reasonable notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is fairly acceptable, or tolerably good, is calling it reasonable.

clue.text: Juvenile not finishing cold food

indicators.note: not finishing drops the last letter

parts.note: a chill is coldness
a dish is a prepared item of food

explanation.surface: A youngster who won't eat up a cold meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenile in its disparaging sense means immature, like a child.

clue.text: Grazing area stops wife entering anyhow

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or pasture, a poetic word for grazing land

indicators.note: entering means the letter goes inside the other word

parts.note: stays means stops, as in stays put

explanation.surface: On a pasture the wife comes in and halts, in any case.
explanation.definitionFit: This dialect adverb means at least, or in any case, much like anyhow.

clue.text: Fashion in which cut is announced?

indicators.note: is announced means said aloud, so the word is read by its sound

parts.note: lawns are mowed, that is cut

explanation.surface: A question about the style in which a garment is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A mode is a style or vogue, so the word is a synonym for fashion.

clue.text: Mournful merriment — false, at last, and true

parts.note: fun is merriment

indicators.note: at last takes only the final letter of false

parts.note: real means true or genuine

explanation.surface: Grief turns out to be fake merriment, but genuine in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Funereal means suited to a funeral, hence gloomy and sorrowful.

clue.text: Irish moss, for example, carried around by bag lady

indicators.note: around means the letters run the other way
carried means the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: Some Irish moss is lugged about by a homeless woman with bags.
explanation.walkthrough: Irish moss, or carrageen, is a red seaweed, not a moss.
explanation.definitionFit: Irish moss is a seaweed, and a seaweed is a type of simple aquatic plant in this class.

clue.text: Taken outside, I have to rest

indicators.note: outside means the past tense of lead goes round the letter

parts.note: led means taken, as in taken by the hand
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Escorted out, I must take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to recline and take a rest.

clue.text: Supporter getting turn in ground with cricket side

indicators.note: ground as past of grind means these letters are crushed into a new order

parts.note: the on side, or leg side, is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A fan taking a spin at the cricket ground with the home team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' is not a cricket ground but the anagram signal; in cricket the on side is the leg side of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A trunnion is a pin or pivot supporting something, such as a cannon, on its mounting.

clue.text: One's beginning online reports about new figures

indicators.note: beginning takes the first letter
about means the web diaries go round the letter

parts.note: blogs are online journals or reports

explanation.surface: Someone starts an online report about new numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Oblongs are rectangles, a kind of geometric figure.

clue.text: US president's misplaced a hole in the ground

indicators.note: misplaced means the letter is moved to another place in the name

parts.note: Jimmy Carter was the 39th US president; the 's stands for has
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American president has lost something in a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a pit or depression in the earth's surface.

clue.text: Modern form of erection

indicators.note: form of means a rearrangement of the following letters

explanation.surface: A new type of building construction.
explanation.definitionFit: Neoteric is a rare adjective meaning recent or new-fangled.

clue.text: Financial backers beheaded by European communist

indicators.note: beheaded removes the first letter

parts.note: angels are investors who back a theatrical show

explanation.surface: Investors get their heads cut off by a Continental red.
explanation.definitionFit: Friedrich Engels co-wrote The Communist Manifesto with Karl Marx.

clue.text: Question for cook

definitions.meaning: to cook under direct radiant heat

explanation.definitionFit: Police interrogate suspects intensely, and chefs cook meat under a radiant heater; one verb covers both.

clue.text: Colour of swan for all to see in fantastic ballet

parts.note: a cob is a male swan

indicators.note: in places the film letter inside the rearranged letters
fantastic means the letters of ballet are wildly rearranged

parts.note: U is the British film rating for films suitable for everyone

explanation.surface: The colour of the swan, on view to all, in a magical ballet like Swan Lake.
explanation.definitionFit: This deep blue pigment is made from compounds of a metallic element, a recognised shade.

clue.text: I'm the proprietor of a sound Scottish island

indicators.note: sound here means the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: being a proprietor means I own something, so the phrase is I own a

explanation.surface: A landlord boasts of owning a pleasant Scottish isle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like an adjective, good or healthy, describing the island; it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Iona is a small island in the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.

clue.text: Animals celebrated going west

indicators.note: in an across answer going west means read from right to left

parts.note: sung means celebrated, as in praises sung

explanation.surface: Feted creatures are dying off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going west' is slang for dying, but here it reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnus, or wildebeest, are African antelopes, hence animals.

clue.text: Excellent hand getting sail level

parts.note: a royal is a small sail set above the topgallant on a square-rigger
flush means level, as in flush with the wall

explanation.surface: A good card holding gets a sailor's canvas even.
explanation.walkthrough: In poker this is the top hand, ace to ten of one suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker it is the best possible hand of cards, ace high straight in one suit.
